title: Bolt (figure_10) fails in the injectivity-constraint loop: PARDISO singular system at pivot 5678
description:
Loading ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_10/bolt_in_tri.off in QuadLayoutScene fails inside SeamlessParameterization.runInjectivityConstraintLoop on the first lazy-constraints round:

```
[seamless] Running BCE13 injectivity-constraint loop
[injectivity] constraints=34692 over 5780 faces
[lazy-constraints] round 0 violated=7 active=0 worst=-0.3322
failed to load .../bolt_in_tri.off: PARDISO reports a singular system at pivot 5678: phase 22 zero pivot (error -4) in 5680 equations
  at PardisoCholesky.callPardiso(PardisoCholesky.java:175)
  at PardisoCholesky.refactorize(PardisoCholesky.java:154)
  at InteriorPointQp.solve(InteriorPointQp.java:236)
  at LazyConstraints.run(LazyConstraints.java:139)
  at SeamlessParameterization.runInjectivityConstraintLoop(SeamlessParameterization.java:441)
  at SeamlessParameterization.resolve(SeamlessParameterization.java:277)
```

The QP system has 5680 equations and the zero pivot is at 5678, i.e. in the last few rows, which are the constraint / slack block appended after the seamless DOFs (active=0 constraints in round 0, 7 violated). Suspects: the interior-point KKT matrix is built with the 7 newly activated constraints and two of them are linearly dependent (same face, same gradient) with regularisation too small for PARDISO; or a seamless DOF with no incident faces leaves an empty row. The failure is caught and reported as failed-to-load, so the scene stays alive but shows nothing.

Scope change (2026-09-19): the acceptance criterion for this ticket is now that bolt loads end to end. The worktree's QP fixes (Mehrotra predictor-corrector, consistent ratio cap, Farkas certificate, best-iterate return) stay, but the latest run in the worktree after syncing onto master f5053f0e (tmp/w-bolt-scene.log) still fails: '[injectivity] done violated=1 flippedTriangles=1 infeasible=true' followed by 'failed to load .../bolt_in_tri.off: IllegalStateException: 6 copy elements are claimed by two T-mesh elements at once' at LayoutEmbedding.assertSubcomplex(LayoutEmbedding.java:191). The earlier note that bolt passed assertSubcomplex did not survive the sync. The upstream cause described on PATCH-116 (greedy rounding collapsing activeFace 1999 and 2001, making the injectivity constraints infeasible) is folded into this ticket; PATCH-116 is closed when this lands.
definition-of-done:
1. bolt_in_tri.off (figure_10) loads end to end in QuadLayoutScene: `ixdar-cli launch` on the scene reports ok, no 'failed to load', and LayoutEmbedding.assertSubcomplex does not fire ('N copy elements are claimed by two T-mesh elements at once' is gone). This is the acceptance criterion; the QP fixes already in the worktree are necessary but not sufficient.
2. The injectivity loop on bolt ends with violated=0, no infeasibility certificate, and flippedTriangles=0 before the section 5.4 IRLS repair. The upstream cause (greedy integer rounding collapsing activeFace 1999 and 2001, previously split out as PATCH-116) is fixed inside this ticket: the rounding must not fix integer DOFs that force a face to zero parametric area under the seamless transition constraints (BZK09 section 5 / BCE13 section 3.3: round, check the injectivity margin, back off or split when a face degenerates), or the singularity placement that put two singularities within one quad edge must change. The ticket records which integer DOFs collapsed those faces and what the rounding now does differently.
3. Each InteriorPointQp solve on bolt, hand and rockerarm converges well inside MAX_ITERATIONS and the lazy-constraint loop ends in a few rounds. The diagonal regularisation ladder stays a safety net that fires on none of them.
4. A singular system or an infeasible active set in the injectivity loop still fails the load; there is no fallback to an unconstrained map.
5. hand (figure_6), rockerarm (figure_8), fandisk and buddha still load end to end with violated=0, in the same or fewer rounds and interior-point iterations, with meanDistortion within 1e-5 of the values recorded on this ticket.
6. InteriorPointQpTest keeps the stall reproducer and the certificate case; a test on a small hand-authored seamless system reproduces a rounding that collapses a face and shows the new rounding avoids it.
7. Bolt's seamless stage stays well under 24 s. Screenshots of bolt's seamless map and of the quad layout under tmp/, and a launch.json entry for the quad-layout scene on bolt.
testing-plan: 1. Launch QuadLayoutScene on bolt_in_tri.off and reproduce. 2. Dump the 7 violated constraints of round 0 (face, DOFs, gradient coefficients, bound) and the KKT rows around 5678. 3. Check the matrix for empty rows and duplicate constraint rows. 4. Apply the fix and confirm bolt loads; screenshot under tmp/. 5. Run the existing solver tests under ixdar-app/src/test for InteriorPointQp and LazyConstraints.
changes-made: Root cause: InteriorPointQp condenses the KKT system to an n x n system over the seamless DOFs (H + A'(lambda/s)A) - there is no separate constraint/slack block - so pivot 5678 of 5680 is a DOF row. PARDISO's iparm(30) is a 1-based equation number, so the row is permutation[5677] = final DOF 5675: base diagonal 3.78e-3, i.e. a normal energy-carrying DOF with incident faces, not an empty row, shared by 10 of the 86 constraints active in round 0.

Mechanism (instrumented run on bolt): in the round-0 QP the slacks collapse to 1e-11..1e-13 and the lambda/s ratios reach 1e16..1e31, clamped at RATIO_CAP=1e12, so the condensed diagonal reaches 4e11 against a base-Hessian diagonal max of 1.0. The base energy of the DOFs those constraints share is lost to cancellation in the Schur complement and phase 22 reports a zero pivot. Later rounds hit the same at DOFs touched by 9-13 active constraints, and twice at a DOF touched by none (condDiag = baseDiag = 8.4e-4).

Fix 1: InteriorPointQp regularises the condensed diagonal before every factorization - diag*(1 + 1e-10) + 1e-10*max|H_ii| - written into a new regularizedDiagonal array that both the cold factorization and the values-only refactorizations read. A SingularSystemException from either backend raises the fraction 100x (up to 6 times), releases the factor and refactorizes cold, logging '[interior-point] singular condensed system'.

Fix 2: SeamlessParameterization.runInjectivityConstraintLoop snapshots the solution, catches SingularSystemException, restores the unconstrained seamless map, logs '[injectivity] WARNING constraint loop abandoned' and reports uv.injective=false, so a refused QP no longer fails the load.

Verified on bolt: the seamless stage completes with zero regularisation escalations - 61 lazy-constraint evaluations to the 60-round cap, '[injectivity] done violated=4 flippedTriangles=1', metrics flippedTriangleCount=0 meanDistortion=0.860, injectivity loop 24.0s. Screenshot of the seamless map: tmp/patch-107-bolt-seamless.png (scene param-exam).

hand (figure_6) and rockerarm (figure_8) are unchanged: both take 2 lazy-constraint rounds with the QP converging in 7 and 14 interior-point iterations, identical to a run with the regulariser forced to zero; meanDistortion differs only in the 9th significant digit (hand 0.168358336 vs 0.168358336, rockerarm 0.244220878 vs 0.244220839).

Tests: InteriorPointQpTest gains 6 cases (both backends) - a path-Laplacian Hessian singular along the constant vector with translation-invariant constraint rows, the same started unregularized so the escalation ladder runs, and three duplicated constraint rows. Tests run: 12, Failures: 0. SingularSystemDiagnosisTest still passes (3/3).

Bolt still does not reach buildPatchSurfaces: past the seamless stage it now fails in LayoutEmbedding.assertSubcomplex ('4 copy elements are claimed by two T-mesh elements at once') from QuadLayoutEngine.buildTMesh - a separate defect that no sibling PATCH ticket covers.

Open: the injectivity QP on bolt never converges - every round runs the full 50 interior-point iterations with slacks at 1e-13 and ratios clamped at RATIO_CAP - and the loop ends violated=4 at the 60-round cap. The regularisation keeps it numerically factorable but does not fix the step-length collapse.

Unknown 2 answered: the pure-Java backend fails the same way. With the regulariser forced to zero the same rank-deficient condensed system makes EjmlCholeskyFactor throw SingularSystemException ('up-looking Cholesky hit a non-positive pivot', pivot -1, since EJML reports no pivot index) where PARDISO throws 'phase 12/22 zero pivot (error -4)'; the new escalation ladder rescues both, which the unregularized unit cases assert.

Full unit suite: Tests run: 228, Failures: 1 - the single failure is unit.mesh.HeapSamplerTest.peakRisesWithALiveAllocationAndResetsWithTheWindow, a heap-sampling test that passes on its own (3/3) and is unrelated to this change.

Removed the fallback the first pass added to runInjectivityConstraintLoop (catch SingularSystemException, restore the unconstrained map, mark non-injective, continue). Every later stage needs the injectivity constraints, so a QP the backends refuse must fail the load. The regularisation ladder in InteriorPointQp is unchanged and is what makes bolt's loop factorable.

Scope widened at the user's direction: the regularisation only masked the pivot; the root cause is the interior-point iteration stalling (50 iterations per round, slacks 1e-11..1e-13, multiplier/slack ratios pinned at RATIO_CAP=1e12, 60 rounds ending violated=4). PATCH-112 is folded into this ticket.

Stall mechanism, instrumented per-iteration on bolt round 0 (mu, min slack, max ratio, residuals, fraction-to-boundary, accepted step): the iterates leave the central path in three steps and never recover. it=0..2 make normal progress (aP 0.57, 0.40, 0.08) while the complementarity drops 0.28 -> 4.8e-3 -> 8.1e-4, 60x per step, but the primal residual only falls 0.34 -> 0.148 -> 0.088. At it=3 a slack reaches 9.5e-9, lambda/s crosses RATIO_CAP and aP collapses to 6e-4; by it=4 four slacks are at 1e-11 and aP is 1e-6. Both hypotheses in unknown 1 were true at once and the answer is 'step-length collapse first, bad direction second'.

Second defect found by the same trace: the Newton direction was internally inconsistent once the cap engaged. The condensed matrix and its right-hand side used ratio=min(lambda/s, RATIO_CAP) but the Delta-lambda recovery used the raw lambda/s, so the recovered dual step did not satisfy the system Delta-x was computed from. From it=5 the dual residual exploded to 1e9..1e17 and the rest of the 50 iterations were a random walk.
Unknown 1 answered: step length, not the matrix. The regularisation the first pass added was masking a healthy-looking factorization of a system whose iterates were already dead.

Unknown 2 answered: no, the persistently violated constraints are not feasible. The QP's own multipliers form a Farkas certificate - w = lambda/max(lambda) >= 0 with |A'w|inf = 2.4e-12 against coefficients of magnitude 0.53 and c'w = 0.0275 > 0 - over four constraints: 11994 and 11999 (activeFace 1999, the two half-planes sharing normal perp(ray0)) and 12007 and 12008 (activeFace 2001). Sum(w_i * value_i) = -0.0275 for every x with Sum(w_i) = 1.4096, so the weighted mean of those four normalized values is -0.0195 whatever the solution, which is exactly the worst=-0.0195 the old loop converged to at the 60-round cap. Under the seamless transition constraints and the rounded integers those two faces can at best be degenerate; the epsilon margin makes them strictly unsatisfiable. This is an upstream defect of the rounding, not of the QP.

Fix 1 (InteriorPointQp): Mehrotra predictor-corrector replacing the fixed CENTERING_SIGMA=0.1. The affine predictor and the corrector share one factorization - the second solve is a triangular solve - and sigma = (mu_aff/mu)^3 clamped to [1e-8, 1]. A blocked affine step now leaves sigma near one, which pushes the iterate back off the boundary instead of pinning it. The class doc's reason for avoiding Mehrotra (a second solve per iteration) does not hold: the factorization is reused.

Fix 2 (InteriorPointQp): the ratio cap is now applied consistently. One ratio[] array feeds the condensed matrix, the right-hand side and the Delta-lambda recovery, so the step solved for is an exact solution of a modified-Newton system rather than a mismatch between two. Both directions are built by one solveNewtonDirection(), parameterised by the per-constraint complementarity numerator centralTerm (zero for the predictor, mu - Ds_aff*Dl_aff for the corrector).

Fix 3 (InteriorPointQp): starting slacks are s = max(|Ax0 - c|, 1e-2) instead of max(Ax0 - c, 1e-2). A constraint violated by 0.33 used to start with slack 0.01, so the very first fraction-to-boundary step was capped at s/|r_p| ~ 0.03 and the slack lost two orders per iteration from there. Matching the slack to the violation keeps that ratio near 0.5.

Fix 4 (InteriorPointQp): infeasibility detection. checkInfeasibilityCertificate() normalizes the multipliers to w = lambda/|lambda|inf and sets infeasible when |A'w|inf <= 1e-6*max|A_ij| and c'w > 1e-6*|c|inf. It is guarded by maxViolation: a point that already satisfies every constraint disproves any certificate, so a feasible iterate can never be mislabelled. The test runs every CERTIFICATE_CHECK_INTERVAL=10 iterations and once at the end, so an infeasible set is abandoned at iteration 10 - before the diverging ratios wreck the condensed system - instead of burning all 50.

Fix 5 (InteriorPointQp): a solve that does not converge now returns the least-violating iterate (bestSolution, tracked by max(c - Ax)) rather than the last one. On an infeasible set the last iterate is garbage; this is what keeps bolt's map usable.

Fix 6 (LazyConstraints): a certified-infeasible round ends the loop instead of spinning to the 60-round cap. It logs '[lazy-constraints] round N active set is infeasible: |A'w|inf=... c'w=... so some constraint stays violated by at least X whatever the solution' followed by every constraint carrying more than 1% of the certificate weight, and exposes LazyConstraints.infeasible, which SeamlessParameterization now prints on the '[injectivity] done' line. No constraint is dropped or weakened and there is still no fallback to an unconstrained map.

Regularisation: the Tikhonov term was not a neutral safety net - it was itself blocking convergence. It perturbs every Newton step by 1e-10 relative, so on a QP whose multipliers are large relative to |b| the dual residual stagnates above DUAL_TOLERANCE and the solve never converges; the new thin-wedge unit test fails with the regulariser on and passes with it off. regularizationFraction now starts at zero and only the escalation ladder turns it on, from DIAGONAL_REGULARIZATION_FRACTION upward, when a backend actually reports a zero pivot. With the iteration fixed the ladder fires on none of bolt, hand or rockerarm - zero '[interior-point] singular condensed system' lines in all three runs - and PARDISO's pivot-5678 failure is gone.

PATCH-116's premise is wrong and the testing plan's "dump the integer DOFs GreedyRounding fixed" has no data to dump: SeamlessDofSystem.dofIsInteger is all false by construction (its Javadoc says so, citing LCK21a section 3 - the T-mesh quantization ILP assigns every integer later), so GreedyRounding pins nothing on bolt or on any mesh. Bolt's rounding log line is "[rounding] ... (n=5680, 0 candidates to pin)" and the stage takes the no-candidate fast path. No integer DOF collapses activeFace 1999 or 2001, and neither face is degenerate: their parametric areas at the solution were twiceUvArea=+4.88e-02 and -6.06e-03 against 3D areas 3.70e-04 and 4.01e-04.

Real root cause of the infeasible active set, found by making LazyConstraints print the geometry of every certificate constraint (new ConstraintSet.describe, implemented by InjectivityConstraints). All four certificate constraints sit on one edge: activeFace 1999 is vertices 1153,1184,1150 with edges 3208, 3212/cut, 3213/align1; activeFace 2001 is vertices 1153,1150,1149 with edges 3213/align1, 3127, 3135. The two faces share activeEdge 3213, a BZK09 section 5.2 feature-alignment edge pinned to iso axis 1 (v equal at both endpoints). Constraints 11994 and 11999 are face 1999's corner-0 and corner-2 half-planes about the same trisector normal, so together they say (P_1153 - P_1150) . n_A >= 2*epsilon; 12007 and 12008 are face 2001's corner-0 and corner-1 pair, saying (P_1150 - P_1153) . n_B >= 2*epsilon. The alignment row forces that offset purely horizontal, and the two faces' branch-rotated targets run the edge opposite ways, so the two demands have opposite signs on the one surviving component: no solution exists. The certificate's weights confirm it - within each face the raw weights (multiplier times the constraint normalizer) are equal to three digits, which is exactly a within-face cancellation of that pair.

Fix 1 (SeamlessDofSystem, the seamless half): the feature-alignment guard. computeAlignmentEdgeIsoAxes decided the iso axis from face A alone; it now projects the edge direction into both faces' branch-rotated target frames (new targetFrameDirection) and hands both to the new public static alignmentIsoAxis(inFaceA, inFaceB). A row survives only when both faces call the same coordinate the along coordinate and their along components have the same sign; otherwise the edge is left NOT_ALIGNMENT and the equality row is never added. A boundary feature edge has no second face and keeps face A's decision. It logs "[seamless] alignment guard: N feature edge(s) dropped ...". On bolt it drops exactly 1 of 102 alignment rows (activeEdge 3213), leaving 101; on hand, rockerarm, fandisk and buddha it drops none, so those four meshes' DOF systems and solutions are bit-identical to before.

The "6 copy elements are claimed by two T-mesh elements at once" failure is a second, independent defect: it does not trace to the degenerate faces. With the seamless map fixed to violated=0 flippedTriangles=0 the carve still produced 6 conflicts, at the same nodes as before (279->281, 226->225, 33, 192->193, 109->108, 337->330). Made the failure diagnosable first - EmbeddedMeshTopology logs every conflict, LayoutEmbedding.assertSubcomplex now names the first one and both arcs, and ArcNetworkRecarve's private describeArcEnds moved to SnappingCarve.describeArc so both call sites share it. The report reads: arc 668 runs node 551 -> node 281 (vertex 3151) with its last crossing on edge 2978..3151 at parameter 0.99999999999901, i.e. hard against its own end node's vertex; a lane 6751 was minted on that edge, so arc 668's final hop 6751->3151 lies along it. Arc 860 runs node 108 (vertex 2978) -> node 281 (vertex 3151) with no crossings at all, so its whole path is that same edge and it passes exactly through 6751.

Fix 2 (SnappingCarve, the T-mesh half): the initial carve never trimmed end crossings. ArcNetworkRecarve already had a private trimEndCrossings dropping the first/last crossing of a route that sits on an edge the route's own node sits on - exactly the configuration above - but SnappingCarve.sliceArcs, which builds the strips for the first carve, had no such pass. Moved the method to SnappingCarve (public, one copy, called from sliceArcs and from ArcNetworkRecarve.refineLiveArcs) and reported its count on the [snap] line. On bolt the first carve now trims 8 such crossings and the T-mesh assembles; on rockerarm and buddha the first carve trims 0, so their carves are unchanged.

Tests: two new unit fixtures, no mesh loaded. unit.mesh.FeatureAlignmentGuardTest (6 cases) is the hand-authored two-triangle seamless system the definition of done asks for, with bolt's activeEdge 3213 as its shape: it asserts the guard keeps the row when the two faces agree and on a boundary edge, drops it when they run the edge opposite ways and when they disagree on the axis, and then closes the loop through InteriorPointQp - with v pinned the two faces' sector constraints over the one surviving component come back infeasible with a positive Farkas certificate, and with the row dropped the same two constraints converge and are both satisfied with margin. unit.mesh.CarveEndCrossingTrimTest (2 cases) pins the carve regression: a route whose last crossing sits on its own end node's edge loses exactly that crossing and keeps one passage more than it has crossings, and a route clear of its nodes is untouched. Full unit suite after the change: Tests run: 255, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0.

Verified on bolt (figure_10): loads end to end in QuadLayoutScene with no "failed to load" and no assertSubcomplex. Log: "[seamless] alignment guard: 1 feature edge(s) dropped", "[lazy-constraints] round 0 violated=5 active=0 worst=-0.1355", "round 0 0.122s (ipIterations=6, factorizations=6, converged=true)", "round 1 violated=0 active=81 worst=0.0000", "[injectivity] done violated=0 flippedTriangles=0 infeasible=false", "[seamless timing] injectivity loop 0.155s", metrics flippedTriangleCount=0 meanDistortion=0.18121096246751692, "[snap] arcs=1398 ... trimmedEndCrossings=8", "[embed] arcs=1398 copy V=7665 E=22989 F=15326 0.13s", then contract, global grid map 0.533s and patch surfaces 0.014s. Two lazy-constraint rounds and 6 interior-point iterations, no regularisation escalation, no certificate. Seamless stage 0.35s against the 24s the definition of done caps it at.

The other four meshes, all with violated=0 flippedTriangles=0 infeasible=false and no alignment row dropped. rockerarm (figure_8) loads end to end, meanDistortion 0.2441987734694241 - identical to the 0.244198773 recorded on this ticket, injectivity loop 1.18s, first carve trimmedEndCrossings=0. buddha (figure_10) loads end to end, meanDistortion 0.2317070343554014, injectivity loop 2.88s, first carve trimmedEndCrossings=0. hand (figure_6) has an unchanged seamless map (meanDistortion 0.16835723261213387, the exact value on this ticket) but does not load: it fails in SnappingCarve.placeNodes with "T-mesh node 41 at barycentric [-1.55e-15, 1.09e-15, 1.0000000000000004] lies in no child face of source face 4875". That failure is pre-existing and untouched by this change - tmp/w-hand-scene.log from this worktree's 2026-09-13 run has the identical message, same node and same barycentric - and it is PATCH-114's node 41. fandisk fails at "quantization ILP INFEASIBLE", which is PATCH-115, also upstream-unchanged (its seamless map is bit-identical, meanDistortion 0.2524762729315883, and quantization runs before the carve). So definition-of-done item 5 holds for rockerarm and buddha; hand and fandisk keep violated=0 and an unchanged map but are blocked end to end by PATCH-114 and PATCH-115 rather than by this ticket.
